chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Husayn from Sama'a from Abu Basir said:

I asked him about the sick person: does the woman hold something for him to prostrate upon? He said, 'No, unless he is in need and has no one else, and there is nothing forbidden by Allah except that He has made it permissible for one who is in need of it.'
And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhayna from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about the sick person. He said, 'He prostrates on the ground, or on a hand-fan, or on a miswak stick. Raising it is better than gesturing. Those who disliked prostrating on the hand-fan did so because of the idols that were worshipped besides Allah, and we have never worshipped anything other than Allah. So prostrate on the hand-fan, or on a miswak, or on a stick.'
ai.seo_question: What should a sick person do if they cannot prostrate on the ground during prayer?
ai.summary: These narrations from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* detail the fiqh of *salat al-mudtir* (prayer of necessity), establishing that a sick person may prostrate on any clean surface, such as a hand-fan (*mirwah*) or stick, if the ground is inaccessible. The scholars clarify that the historical aversion to prostrating on fans was due to their association with idols, not the material itself, thereby validating their use for worship. This ruling underscores the principle of *al-darurat tubih al-mahzurat* (necessity permits the prohibited) when no other option exists.
